what_its_for: Posaconazole is an antifungal medicine used to prevent or treat serious fungal infections. It is often used in people whose immune systems are weakened, such as those receiving chemotherapy or organ transplants. It works by stopping the fungus from growing and spreading in your body.
how_to_take: Posaconazole comes in three forms: a liquid (oral suspension), delayed-release tablets, and an injection given by a healthcare provider. Take the liquid form with a full meal or a nutritional supplement to help your body absorb it properly. Swallow the delayed-release tablets whole — do not crush, chew, or break them. Take tablets with food. Always take this medicine at the same time each day and complete the full course of treatment, even if you feel better.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your condition, weight, and the form of medicine you are taking. A common adult dose for prevention of fungal infections is 200 mg (5 mL of liquid) three times a day with meals, OR one 300 mg delayed-release tablet twice a day on the first day, then once a day after that. Never change your dose without talking to your doctor or pharmacist first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store the liquid (oral suspension) at room temperature between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Do not freeze the liquid. Store the delayed-release tablets at room temperature, away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Keep all forms of this medicine out of reach of children. Do not use after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking posaconazole with certain other medicines without your doctor's approval, as it can interact with many drugs including blood thinners, heart medications, cholesterol medicines, and seizure medicines. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice as it may affect how the medicine works. Do not drink excessive alcohol while taking this medicine. Tell your doctor about all medicines, vitamins, and herbal supplements you take before starting posaconazole.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: yellowing of your skin or eyes (signs of liver problems), dark urine or pale stools, severe stomach pain or nausea, irregular or fast heartbeat or chest pain, signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing, unusual tiredness or weakness, vision changes, or any new or worsening symptoms. Also contact your doctor if your fungal infection does not seem to be improving.
when_it_works: Posaconazole starts working soon after you begin taking it, but it may take several days to weeks before you notice a full improvement in your symptoms. It is important to keep taking the medicine for as long as your doctor prescribes, even if you feel better early, to make sure the infection is completely gone.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Posaconazole may harm an unborn baby. Tell your doctor immediately if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Effective birth control should be used during treatment. Children: The safety and dosing in children under 13 years old may differ — your doctor will advise on appropriate use. Elderly patients: No major dose adjustments are usually needed, but your doctor will monitor you closely. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as your dose may need to be adjusted or your condition monitored more carefully.
